field_accounts.quote: Were you approached by community and/or political party representatives?
field_accounts.account: Respondent-facing yes/no contact item with options '0 = No | 1 = Yes'; records whether any approach by community or party representatives occurred, without specifying which actor, timing, or who initiated.

field_accounts.quote: Did you feel threatened during the interview?
field_accounts.account: Respondent-reported feeling of threat tied to the interview episode; '0 = No | 1 = Yes' cannot distinguish feeling threatened from being threatened, nor identify source or severity.

field_accounts.quote: Were you physically threatened during the interview?
field_accounts.account: Respondent-reported physical-threat item; framing as a question to the respondent ('Were you physically threatened') implies respondent-side report, distinct from Q106D's felt-threat wording and from any interviewer observation.

field_accounts.quote: What was the respondent's attitude toward you during the interview?
field_accounts.account: Interviewer-reported evaluation of respondent demeanor, three-way '1 = Honest | 2 = In between | 3 = Misleading'; it is an interviewer judgment about the respondent, not a respondent self-report.

rival_readings.reading: Q106C contact was with community representatives only, not political party representatives.
rival_readings.why: The stem uses 'community and/or political party representatives', so the metadata permits either or both actors, but the single dichotomy cannot separate them.

rival_readings.reading: Q106C contact was initiated by the respondent versus imposed on the respondent.
rival_readings.why: 'Were you approached by' describes being approached without direction of initiative or consent, and no follow-up item is supplied.

rival_readings.reading: Q106D and Q106E are redundant measures of the same threat.
rival_readings.why: 'Did you feel threatened' versus 'Were you physically threatened' differ in modality (felt vs physical) yet the packet supplies no routing to establish independence or nesting.

rival_readings.reading: Q109F reflects an actual truthfulness outcome rather than an interviewer impression.
rival_readings.why: The item asks the interviewer 'What was the respondent's attitude toward you', an evaluative perception with 'In between' as a middle option; it does not record verified honesty.

rival_readings.reading: Q109F could be treated as parallel to the Q106 threat items as a respondent experience.
rival_readings.why: The Q109F stem is interviewer-addressed ('toward you during the interview'), so it must remain interviewer-side; the Q106D/E items are respondent-addressed ('Did you feel'/'Were you').

surviving_positive.claim: An interviewer-side evaluative record exists: the respondent's demeanor was rated on the 'Honest | 2 = In between | 3 = Misleading' scale.
surviving_positive.quote: What was the respondent's attitude toward you during the interview?
surviving_positive.note: Survives because the interviewer-side role and three-point evaluation are explicit in the stem and options, independent of whether the rating is accurate.

surviving_positive.claim: A binary reporter of approach-contact exists at the respondent level.
surviving_positive.quote: Were you approached by community and/or political party representatives?
surviving_positive.note: What survives is only that some approach is dichotomously coded '0 = No | 1 = Yes'; actor identity and initiative remain open.

exact_discriminants.would_decide: A subgroup or separate item distinguishing community representatives from political party representatives.
Routing or filter text showing whether Q106E is asked conditional on Q106D, or an independent overlap item.
Codebook note defining 'In between' as uncertainty versus partial honesty.

exact_discriminants.dependency: temporal/route relation between contact and interview items
exact_discriminants.would_decide: Interview-sequence or form metadata placing Q106C before or after the interview episode.

limits: Metadata only: no respondent-level co-occurrence, frequencies, or cross-tabulations are supplied, so no association between Q106C contact and any threat or honesty item is observed.
No routing or skip logic is in the packet; whether Q106E was asked only after Q106D, and whether any item was asked of all respondents, is unobserved and stated as such.
Absence of a discriminating item in the packet is not evidence that the construct is unmeasured in the full R9 instrument; it is only unobserved here.
Q109F must not be relabeled as respondent experience because the stem is interviewer-addressed; any merged scale mixing Q109F with Q106D/E would cross role boundaries.

foil_transfer_check.check: Would a plainly plausible foil survive the same packet?
foil_transfer_check.foil: Respondent-reported fear item, parallel in role to Q106D.
foil_transfer_check.result: Transfers only for Q106D, not Q109F
foil_transfer_check.quote_used: Did you feel threatened during the interview?
foil_transfer_check.explanation: The foil's role logic matches the respondent-addressed Q106D wording ('Did you feel'), while Q109F's interviewer-addressed stem ('the respondent's attitude toward you') blocks transfer; this confirms role identity is decided by wording, not by topic proximity.
